payload.title: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows
payload.description: Adopt gomion's generated CI and Release workflows in go-fsfix by running gomion repo setup, committing the result, and confirming the first Actions runs show no warnings or notices
payload.plan:
# Plan: adopt gomion's generated workflows in go-fsfix

1. Use a gomion build that includes E-2454's `gomion repo` commands.
2. In go-fsfix, run `gomion repo setup`. It raises each go.mod below Go 1.27 and tidies it, then writes .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml.
3. Run `gomion repo setup --check`; it must report the repo up to date.
4. Run each module's tests locally with GOWORK=off.
5. Commit the generated workflows and the raised go.mod/go.sum files together.

After the land: push, then read the annotations on the first Test run (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/check-runs/<job id>/annotations` for each job), and on the next Release run once there is one. Each must show zero warnings and zero notices; any that remain are fixed in gomion's templates, not here.

ops.statement: go-fsfix's .github/workflows/test.yml and release.yml are exactly what gomion repo workflows generates, and gomion repo setup --check reports the repo up to date
Every go.mod in go-fsfix declares go 1.27 or later and is tidy
Does not hand-edit the generated workflow files; a change goes into gomion's templates
After the push, the first Test run and the next Release run show zero Actions warnings and zero notices

payload.title: Exclude Endless commits from release notes
payload.description: Exclude commits that change only .endless/ files from the commit list in go-fsfix's GitHub release notes
payload.plan: In .github/workflows/release.yml, add `':(exclude).endless'` to the pathspec of each `git log` that builds the release notes' commit list, as go-dt's release.yml does. Check with `git log <prev-tag>..HEAD --oneline -- . ':(exclude).endless'` that the Endless commits drop out.
payload.context: go-fsfix's Release workflow lists every commit since the previous tag in the GitHub release notes, including hundreds of Endless commits (ledger entries, task mirrors, lessons) that touch only .endless/. Mike, 2026-10-29: they bury the commits that matter, and he would otherwise hand-edit every release description. gomion's generated Release workflow already excludes them, but E-2472 (adopting it) waits on gomion E-2454, which will not land soon, so this repo's current release.yml gets the one-line fix now.

ops.statement: release.yml's generated release notes leave out commits that change only files under .endless/, using the git log pathspec ':(exclude).endless' as go-dt's release.yml does
Does not otherwise change release.yml or test.yml; E-2472 replaces both with gomion's generated workflows

payload.title: Prepare go-fsfix for a tagged release
payload.description: Prepare go-fsfix for release by committing and pushing pending work, then propose a version and description per module for the owner to tag.
payload.plan:
## Plan
1. Run `git status` and `git log <latest-tag>..HEAD` in the go-fsfix repo; list every module in it that has its own go.mod and tag prefix.
2. Commit any uncommitted work that belongs in the release. Ask the owner about anything unclear instead of guessing.
3. Run the repo's build, vet and tests. Fix or report any failure.
4. Push main to origin. Do not create or push tags.
5. For each module, compare the changes since its latest tag and propose a semver version, explaining whether the change is breaking.
6. Draft a release description for each module.
7. Report the proposed versions and descriptions to the owner. The owner tags and releases when ready.
payload.context: gomion cannot drop its local replace directive for go-fsfix until its work is committed, pushed and tagged on GitHub.

payload.title: Decide how go-fsfix creates real git repository fixtures
payload.description: Decide how go-fsfix fixtures create real git repositories with files committed, and how that composes with its existing dir and file fixtures
payload.context: Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. RepoFixture creates an empty .git directory to simulate a repo and its own comment says git init could be shelled out if anyone ever needs it. gomion needs fixtures that are real git repos (git rev-parse --show-toplevel must work) with files committed, for gompkg, gomcmds and test-module tests. Mike wants go-fsfix to meet most fixture needs without reinventing code; a go-fsfix change, tag and new dependency are infinitesimal costs. The git operations themselves may belong in go-gitutil, with go-fsfix calling them; that split is for this and the go-gitutil brainstorm to settle together.
payload.justification: Mike chose on 2026-11-02 to make go-fsfix broadly reusable rather than hand-roll repo fixtures in gomion; the fixture design is his call

payload.title: Add GoModFixture to go-fsfix
payload.description: Add a GoModFixture that embeds RepoFixture and declares a Go module's go.mod (module path, go version, requires, replaces) so tests get a committed repo with a generated go.mod without hand-writing its text.
payload.context: Mike raised it in the E-2547 brainstorm on 2026-11-06: gomion's tests need committed repos whose root and subdirectories each hold a go.mod, and writing that text by hand in every test is boilerplate. Mike placed the fixture in go-fsfix because a fixture is test code and the go.mod handling that E-2557 extracts from gommod/goutils is production code that should not carry test helpers; test code pulling dependencies is the cheap direction. golang.org/x/mod is already in go-fsfix's graph through go-gitutil. Whether any part of the go.mod description is generic enough for go-dt is E-2557's question; Mike doubts a ModulePath type since its values are DirPath-shaped.

fields.context:
Raised by Mike in gomion E-2540 planning on 2026-11-02. gomion's gompkg tests shell out to git directly (init, add, commit with fixed author env) from a test file; gomion also has its own gommod/gitutils package. Mike: git belongs in go-gitutil. Needed first by go-fsfix real repo fixtures and by gomion tests; mocking git is ruled out because it misses edge cases such as permissions.

Scope added from the go-fsfix brainstorm E-2547 (settled with Mike on 2026-11-06; its outcome holds the design). go-fsfix's RepoFixture now always creates a real repository and gains AddClone and AddWorktree, so the fixture operations go-gitutil must offer are: init with a branch name, forced add of every file, commit with a message and ident, clone, and worktree-add on a new branch. Ident is dt.Mailbox (a Name plus a dt.EmailAddress), which go-dt gains in a task filed from E-2547; go-gitutil defines no identity type of its own and names the field or parameter Ident. The add operation sets advice.addEmbeddedRepo=false so a fixture repo nested in another is recorded as an embedded repository without git's advice message. go-fsfix keeps the *Repo it used and returns it from RepoFixture.Repo(), so init must hand back a usable Repo without a second rev-parse.

Raised by Mike on 2026-11-03 in the E-2546 brainstorm. gompkg's repo setup test has a three-line goModFile(modPath, goVersion) helper that concatenates a go.mod body; the plain go.mod tree fixtures in replace_management, require_check, gogit module_scope and the test module do similar by hand. Mike: this should be standardised in an external package extracted from gommod/goutils rather than live in go-fsfix, which is filesystem-generic and should not know Go. Building on modfile lets the same package emit require and replace lines for fixtures that exercise replace management.

Open question added from the go-fsfix brainstorm E-2547 on 2026-11-06: does a module path earn a go-dt type (dt.ModulePath), or does it stay here? Mike's position: Go-related types are admissible in go-dt (Go's own stdlib carries Go AST types), but a module path may not differ enough from a DirPath to earn one. The differences: for `go get` to fetch it, the first element must contain a dot because it is read as a host (`github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt` fetches; `myorg/mylib` fails with "malformed module path: missing dot in first path element"; stdlib paths such as `net/http` are the deliberate exception), and a major version 2 or higher must appear as a `/vN` suffix that matches the tag (`github.com/mikeschinkel/go-dt/v2` with tag v2.0.0; `/v1` and `/v0` are invalid). go-dt has no dependencies, so a dt.ModulePath would validate by hand rather than through x/mod's module.CheckPath. GoModFixture (E-2564) in go-fsfix consumes whatever this task produces.
